title: Weight is the gravitational force, mass times g
summary: Weight is the gravitational force on an object, equal to its mass times the local gravitational acceleration.
body: OpenStax Physics defines weight as the force of gravity on a mass. From the second law, if the only force is that pull, weight equals mass times g, and the direction is the direction of the pull, usually called down. NASA Glenn's guide states the same relation: weight is mass times the gravitational acceleration. On Earth the textbook uses 9.80 metres per second squared in an example, so a 1.0 kilogram object weighs 9.8 newtons there. A standards table's exact conventional value is a different card. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. The Glenn page was last updated 20 November 2023.
